11 A particle is situated at rest between two metal plates X and Y.
A potential difference (p.d.) is then applied across the plates and produces the electric field
shown.
X
Y
particle
electric
field
The particle moves towards plate X when the p.d. is applied.
What could be the particle?
A
alpha-particle
B
electron
C
neutron
D
proton

hints: Look at the diagram arrows between plate X on the left and plate Y on the right - the electric field points from X toward Y.
Recall that the force on a charge in a uniform field is $F = qE$, with positive charge pushed along the field and negative charge pushed opposite to the field.
Compare the movement toward plate X, opposite to the field, with the charges of alpha-particle $+2e$, proton $+e$, neutron $0$ and electron $-e$.
walkthrough: The diagram shows uniform field lines starting at plate X and ending at plate Y, so the electric field direction is from X to Y and plate X is positive.
For a charge $q$ in electric field strength $E$, the force is $F = qE$. A positive $q$ feels a force in the field direction, while a negative $q$ feels a force opposite to the field direction.
The particle starts at rest but moves toward plate X, which is opposite to the field direction from X to Y. Therefore the force on it is opposite to $E$ and its charge $q$ must be negative.
Of the particles listed, only the negatively charged electron fits a negative charge that moves opposite to the field toward the positive plate. This is option B

A.explanation: An alpha-particle has charge $+2e$, so the force $F = qE$ would be in the direction of the field toward plate Y, not toward plate X.

B.explanation: An electron has charge $-e$, so the force is opposite to the field direction and pushes it toward plate X.

C.explanation: A neutron has zero charge, so $F = qE = 0$ and it would remain at rest between the plates.

D.explanation: A proton has charge $+e$, so the force would be along the field toward plate Y, not toward plate X.
